For the State : Mr. S.K. Srivastava, App

--------
05/ 14.10.2022 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2.  The instant criminal revision application is directed against the judgment dated 27.04.2004,
passed by learned 2nd Additional Sessions Judge, Hazaribagh, whereby the Cr. Appeal No. 17 of 1992, preferred by the petitioner has been dismissed and the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 04.03.1992 in Case No. G- 23 of 1990, T.R. No. 626 of 1992, passed by the learned S.D.J.M., Hazaribagh, whereby the petitioner was convicted and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for six months under Section 16 (1) a (i) & (ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/- and in default of payment of fine to undergo R.I. for two months,
has been affirmed.
3. The prosecution case in brief is based upon the report submitted by the Sanitary-cum-Food Inspector, Kuju Anchal.
According to the prosecution report when he along with other staff inspected the shop of the petitioner they found prepared food stuffs kept exposed for sale.
It is said that on demand the petitioner did not show the licence.
Several persons were present in the shop taking meal and purchasing sweets etc.
Thereafter, Food Inspector prepared the prosecution report obtained sanction and filed the prosecution report.
Thereafter, cognizance has been taken for the said offence; for which the petitioner pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
After trial, the petitioner was found guilty for the offence and was convicted and his appeal was also rejected by the learned appellate court.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the petitioner confines his argument on the question of sentence and submits that the petitioner remained in custody for about 80 days and he is the only earning member of his family and sending him back to prison will hamper his entire family and during entire period of bail,
he never misused the privilege of bail, as such the sentence may be modified.
5. Learned counsel for the State supported the judgment and submits that there is no error in the findings given by the Courts below.
As such, the conviction cannot be set aside.

6. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and after going through the impugned judgments including the lower courts records and keeping in mind the limited submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner and also the scope of revisional jurisdiction, I am not inclined to interfere with the finding of given by the courts below and as such the judgment of conviction passed by the learned trial court and upheld by the learned appellate court is, hereby sustained.
7.

So far as sentence is concerned, it is apparent from record that the incident is of the year 1990 and 32 years have elapsed and the petitioner must have suffered the rigors of litigation for the last 32 years.
Further, petitioners remained in custody for about 80 days and during entire period of bail he never misused the privilege of bail.
8. In a situation of this nature, I am of the opinion that no fruitful purpose would be served by sending the petitioner back to prison.
9. Thus, the sentence passed by the trial court and upheld by the appellate court is hereby modified to the extent that the petitioner is sentenced to undergo for the period already undergone.
10. With the aforesaid observation and modification in sentence only, the instant criminal revision application stands disposed of.
11. The petitioner shall be discharged from the liability of his bail bonds.

12. Let the copy of this order be communicated to the court below.
13.
Let the lower court record be sent back to the court concerned forthwith.

(Deepak Roshan, J.) Pramanik/
